reason: The existing fixed high-frequency detector can miss events dominated by low/middle frequencies. Add a separate selectable detector; retain the original high-frequency default and its evidence.
known_checks: A low/mid Gaussian-windowed two-tone impact over a constant broadband floor is missed by the high detector and found by low_mid.
Changing stereo polarity preserves candidate times/powers; mono and duplicated stereo agree.
Constant tones, constant broadband power and silence do not establish impacts.
Existing A92 and new F3 high-frequency585 candidates remain exact, including original contrasts/windows.
Actual workbench selection/history/export retains detector identity and original context; no automatic physical label or fit.
Invalid detector requests preserve the existing project and reject cleanly.
Real C event preview and all runtime/voice sources remain unchanged.
limits: A complementary acoustic detector is not a backfire classifier or source separator.
No threshold relaxation, background search, cleaning, new media download, global voice promotion or spatial/ADI work.
Any real candidate requires original video/audio context before fitting.
